A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same BADiff paper with readable text, figures, tables, algorithms, equations, and complete Appendices A–H. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Tables 1–6 report original generation-quality, latency, ablation, high-resolution, text-to-image, and teacher-label cost results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Tables 1–6 retain the work's original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons and component ablations.

M1.justification: The entropy conditioning, entropy and calibration losses, stopping policy, training objective, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. Appendix architecture descriptions also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain CIFAR-10, CelebA-HQ, LSUN Church/Bedroom, high-resolution generation, Stable Diffusion text-to-image experiments, and the COCO-val2017 teacher-label timing entry.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5 retain the same comparator membership, including cascade, early-stop, PNDM, and DPM-Solver methods. The ADEPT-to-AdaDiff replacement occurs only in related work, not an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Training budgets, backbones, bitrate intervals, metrics, preprocessing descriptions, and testing procedures are unchanged. Latency evaluation still uses 1,000 test samples after 50 warm-up iterations.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same conditioning, hinge-loss, and calibration-loss ablations. The teacher-label cost analysis and other supplementary analyses contain no added or revised evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing latency-averaging description is unchanged, with no new seed or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–6 and their accompanying findings are retained. For example, BADiff's low-rate CIFAR-10/DDPM FID remains 11.4 and its latency remains 65 ms.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations are unchanged, including the conditional reverse-process derivation, entropy-loss gradient, approximation bound, and complexity analysis in Appendices A–D.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty, bandwidth control, perceptual quality, and computational-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of entropy guidance, ablation outcomes, scalability, and efficiency remain unchanged. Section 5's limitations and future directions, and Appendix H's broader-impact discussion, are also retained.

D1.justification: The code-access statement and technical details in Appendices E–G remain unchanged, including software versions, hardware, training times, codec implementations, architecture specifications, and hyperparameters.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 replaces Liu et al.'s ADEPT (v1 reference 31) with Zhang et al.'s AdaDiff (v2 reference 53). The broader positioning remains unchanged; duplicate consolidation and publication-metadata revisions otherwise retain the same cited works.

P1.justification: The narrative and section order are unchanged. Limited edits add Hanwei Zhu's email and an NSFC funding acknowledgement, replace the related-work method name, and revise or consolidate bibliography entries.

P2.justification: Bibliography consolidation and metadata edits reflow the references across pages 11–14, leaving more blank space on page 14. Figure 1 and the tables retain their content, structure, and placement apart from citation updates.

improvement.justification: Consolidating duplicate references, including entries with conflicting page metadata, and adding contact and funding disclosures modestly improves clarity and transparency. Scientific content is unchanged, and the bibliography cleanup has a limited drawback: the Adam entry drops Jimmy Ba from its author list.
